Explicit three/four constructions prove classification. Bijection through all component bipartitions yields 2^(c-1)s^2 candidates; each duplicated four-block partition corresponds uniquely to an unordered split of components, with exactly two valid pairings, giving 2^(c-2)(2^(c-1)-1). Independently enumerated 174 small regular graphs and checked the duplicate correction on 2,3,4 components. Proof is unrestricted; finite checks are corroborative.

value.rationale: Counts all optimal partitions of a natural domination-derived graph invariant across an infinite connected/disconnected regular class, not merely its maximum. The unexpected correction for multiple component bipartitions is necessary (two disjoint squares have 97 partitions rather than naive 98), and the count depends solely on order and connected-component number even though the underlying graphs vary. Provides a complete enumeration and an explicit multiplicity mechanism, beyond the previously known 3-to-4 numerical bound and cubic case.
